newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda starts V6 engine output in Ohio.
newsitem.headline: Honda starts V6 engine output in Ohio.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it had started production of a V6 3-litre VTEC (Variable Valve Timing & Lift Electronic Control) engine at its plant in Anna, Ohio.
The engine will be installed in its completely new Acura 3.0CL luxury two-door coupe. Honda will start producing the coupe at its East Liberty plant on September 10.
The engine will be also used in Honda's new Minivan, which will be produced from the autumn of 1998 at Honda of Canada Mfg Inc in Alliston, Ontario.
Honda spent $200 million for the new production facilities to produce the V6 engine and an in-line 2.2-litre 4-cylinder engine at the Anna plant.
The plant now produces 1.6- and 2.2-litre car engines and 1.52-litre motorcycle engines. The plant produced 605,127 engines in 1995 and was expected to produce 650,000 in 1996.
Production of the new engine will bring total output to 900,000 in 1998. The new line will increase jobs at the Anna plant by 200 by 1998 from the present 2,300 jobs.
